title: Market Surf Report

conditions.headline: Choppy, Closed-Out Sets After a Six-Day Wipeout
conditions.summary: Nasdaq futures lead a mixed open lower after the S&P 500's sixth straight loss, as doubts over AI spending, Treasury yields above 5% and Fed hike talk keep the tide running out. Asia sold off hard overnight.

sections.title: Futures & Overnight
items: Nasdaq-100 futures were down about 1.1% and S&P 500 futures about 0.4% early Friday; Dow futures edged up 0.2% and Russell futures were flat. Early quotes; sources differed by timestamp.
Thursday the S&P 500 fell 2.0% to about 7,176 for a sixth straight loss, the Dow lost 2.2% and closed under 50,000 for the first time since June, and the Nasdaq Composite fell 2.3%.
Stocks had rallied early Thursday before reversing once Anthropic began trading; the Dow is down about 6% this week and the S&P 500 and Nasdaq about 5%.
The 10-year Treasury yield sits near 5.05%, the dollar index is near a 19-month high around 103.9, and the VIX is near 29, its highest since March.
Gold fell about 2.6% to roughly $3,590 and is down about 8% on the week; bitcoin slipped below $62,000, its lowest since July; WTI crude was near $81 in early trade, though quotes were mixed.
Asia: Japan's Nikkei fell nearly 5% and Korea's Kospi more than 4%, with Samsung and SK Hynix each down over 6%; Hong Kong lost about 2%.
Europe: the Stoxx 600 fell 0.9% Thursday and is headed for its steepest weekly drop since March.

sections.title: Macro & Economic Calendar
items: 7:25 AM CT: Fed Governor Christopher Waller speaks.
9:00 AM CT: Final November University of Michigan consumer sentiment; forecasts cluster around 51, with inflation expectations in focus.
11:15 AM CT: Fed Governor Michael Barr speaks; President Trump is also scheduled to speak around 11:00 AM CT.
Markets now price a quarter-point Fed rate hike in December, with the funds rate at 3.75% to 4%.
Thursday's data was soft: the Philadelphia Fed index sank to 6.3 from 20.9, and jobless claims rose to 203,000, above forecasts.

sections.title: Earnings
items: Intuit fell about 10% after hours following its quarterly report and a deal to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons.
Ross Stores dropped about 5% after hours despite higher third-quarter sales and a raised full-year profit outlook.
Gap rose about 3.6% after hours; third-quarter sales grew 2% to $4.0 billion and earnings beat, but it trimmed its full-year sales outlook to about flat.
Keysight beat fourth-quarter estimates and its shares rose after hours.
Thursday: Walmart slipped 1% despite raising its outlook; Williams-Sonoma fell 15%; PDD jumped 11%.
Few notable companies report after today's close.

sections.title: Stocks in the News
items: ANT (Anthropic): -6.5% — second-day slide after Thursday's debut closed at $97.17, still above the $83 IPO price.
INTU (Intuit): about -10% — quarterly results plus agreement to sell Mailchimp.
ROST (Ross Stores): about -5% — results failed to impress despite a higher profit outlook.
GAP (Gap): about +3.6% — earnings beat and a rebound after hours despite a softer sales outlook.
NVDA (Nvidia): about -2% — AI-spending worries extend a six-day losing streak.
AMD (AMD): fell 7.7% Thursday after a short-seller report questioned its China exposure.
PANW (Palo Alto Networks): rose 6.4% Thursday after lifting its revenue forecast.
Pre-market quotes are early and thin; moves can change by the open.

sections.title: Business News
items: Anthropic's IPO priced at $83 and raised about $81 billion; the stock briefly valued the company near $2 trillion before pulling back.
Intuit agreed to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons.
Palo Alto Networks agreed to buy Applied Compute in an all-stock deal.
BASF ended takeover talks with Evonik, sending Evonik shares down 16% in Europe.
Texas resumed reviewing data center permits, an AI power story worth watching.

sections.title: What to Watch Today
items: Whether the S&P 500 can snap a six-day losing streak, with Thursday's close near 7,176 the line in the sand.
The 9:00 AM CT Michigan sentiment and inflation expectations, plus Fed speakers Waller at 7:25 AM CT and Barr at 11:15 AM CT, for clues on a December hike.
Anthropic and the chip stocks as the gauge of AI sentiment, with the VIX near 29.

script: Cowabunga! This is Surf Daddy, your local Kahuna, live from Surfside USA to all you Trade Wind surfers from the Gulf Coast to the North Shore. It's Friday, November twentieth, twenty twenty-six, and this is your Market Surf Report. Riding shotgun on the cabana deck is Gus the wonder dog, who hasn't missed a Dawn Patrol all week. Give the folks a holler, Gus! Alright, let's check the swell. It's been a gnarly week, friends. The S and P five hundred fell two percent yesterday for a sixth straight loss. The Dow dropped about two percent and closed under fifty thousand for the first time since June. The Nasdaq lost more than two percent. This morning Nasdaq futures are down about one percent, S and P futures are off about four tenths of a percent, and Dow futures are up a hair. These are early quotes, so stay loose. The ten year Treasury yield sits near five point oh five percent. The dollar is near a nineteen month high. Gold fell more than two percent, and bitcoin slipped under sixty two thousand dollars. The fear gauge, the VIX, is near twenty nine. Overseas, Japan's Nikkei dropped nearly five percent and Korea fell more than four. Now the wind and weather. Traders now expect a Fed rate hike in December. Fed Governor Waller speaks at seven twenty five A M Central. The final Michigan consumer sentiment reading lands at nine A M Central. Governor Barr speaks at eleven fifteen. Over on the tide chart, Intuit fell about ten percent after hours on its report and a deal to sell Mailchimp. Ross Stores slid about five percent. But Gap beat on earnings and rose more than three percent after hours. That calls for a treat, Gus! Here you go, buddy! Keysight also beat and moved higher. Checking the lineup, Anthropic is down about six percent in its second day of trading, but it's still above its eighty three dollar I P O price. Nvidia is off about two percent as the A I trade keeps wiping out. A M D fell almost eight percent yesterday on a short seller report. Palo Alto Networks bucked the trend, up six percent on a higher forecast. Beach talk: Anthropic's I P O raised about eighty one billion dollars. Palo Alto agreed to buy Applied Compute. And Texas is back to reviewing data center permits. Sets to watch today: can the S and P snap its losing streak, what does the Michigan survey say about inflation, and how do the A I names hold up.
